# `validation_failed`

The input did not parse, or broke a rule about its own values.

| Status | Title | `type` |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | Validation failed | `https://substrat.net/errors/validation-failed` |

## What it means

The request is wrong as sent. A parse failure carries `errors`: one entry per field, with a dotted `path` (`lines.0.quantity`) and a `message`, and `detail` reads "the input did not parse". A value that parses but contradicts itself, such as an end date before its start, carries no field list. Its `detail` is the sentence.

## When it is returned

- An operation input that fails its declared schema. The host parses every invocation before the operation's handler runs.
- A rule over the input's own values.
- A page cursor replayed into a walk that did not mint it (`reason: cursor_restart`).

## What it carries

- `errors`: One entry per field that failed to parse: `path`, dotted into the input, and `message`.
- `reason`: A slug the refusing module owns, narrowing the code. The platform's own are snake_case, but the wire does not enforce a grammar, so compare it as an opaque string. Branch on it; never show it.

Relayed from a scope store, it may also carry `storeCode` and `storeBody`. See [the body](/errors/#the-body) for the members any problem may carry.

## What to do

Fix the input and send it again; the same body is refused again. With `errors`, show each message against the field its `path` names. With `reason: cursor_restart`, read the first page again without the cursor.

## In `/openapi.json`

Documented on every operation's failure responses.
